appellations.name: Cabrières
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: The largest lieu-dit of the appellation, more than 200 ha of AOC land on the plateau in the north, around the Mont de Cabrières and across into Orange. Deep galets over red clay and the full force of the mistral give ripe, structured Grenache. Château Cabrières takes its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 217.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 50 to 125 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing broadly north (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Bellevue
appellations.summary: The largest climat of Morgon, about 100 ha of AOC land on the higher ground west of Villié-Morgon, at roughly 335 to 410 m. On granite sands rather than the schist of the Côte du Py, it gives lighter, more aromatic Morgon, and its altitude is an asset in hot vintages.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 101.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 335 to 410 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Coudoulet
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A large, flat lieu-dit in Courthézon at the north-eastern edge of the appellation, close to the Perrin family's Château de Beaucastel. The family's Côtes du Rhône Coudoulet de Beaucastel takes its name from the vineyards just outside the Châteauneuf boundary on the other side of the motorway.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 84.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 55 to 60 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Montredon
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A broad lieu-dit in the north-west of the appellation, on a plateau of galets roulés over clay that falls gently toward the west. It is the home of Château Mont-Redon, one of the largest single estates of Châteauneuf-du-Pape, whose Grenache-based reds are a reliable classic.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 78.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 75 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing west to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Labourons
appellations.summary: The largest climat of Fleurie, on the high western slopes toward the hills, at about 350 to 430 m, facing west and south-west; cooler and later-ripening than the village slopes.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 73.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 355 to 425 m, with a mean slope of about 18%, facing broadly west-north-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The high western climats of Fleurie, toward the Avenas hills, were once considered too cool and are now valued for freshness.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Poncié
appellations.summary: A high, granitic climat in the north of Fleurie near Moulin-à-Vent, one of the proposed premier crus. Poncié gives firm, structured Fleurie; Château de Poncié and Pierre-Marie Chermette's Domaine du Vissoux bottle it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 66.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 415 m, with a mean slope of about 20%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Côtes du Py
appellations.summary:
The Côte du Py, a dome of ancient rock east of Villié-Morgon often described as an extinct volcano, is the most famous climat of Morgon. Its blue, metamorphic schist and the crumbly, iron- and manganese-stained rock that locals call *roche pourrie* give the most powerful and mineral Gamay of the Beaujolais, dark-fruited and firm, which 'morgonne' with age, taking on cherry kirsch and earthy notes that recall Pinot Noir.

Jean Foillard's Côte du Py, made with minimal sulphur and aged in old Burgundy barrels, is the classic; Jean-Marc Burgaud, Louis-Claude Desvignes, Mee Godard, Dominique Piron and Louis Jadot's Château des Lumières also bottle it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 69.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 290 to 350 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: 'Morgonner' is a Beaujolais verb for the way old Morgon takes on the character of the cru; the Côte du Py is where it happens most clearly.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Bois-Lauzon
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A flat lieu-dit in the commune of Orange at the northern edge of the appellation, on galets and sand, which gave its name to Mas de Boislauzon.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 61.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 55 to 65 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: In 1923 Baron Pierre Le Roy of Château Fortia drew up local rules for Châteauneuf-du-Pape that became a model for the French AOC system; the AOC followed in 1936.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Terres Blanches
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit whose name, 'white earths', refers to pale limestone and marl soils rather than pebbles. On limestone, Grenache and Mourvèdre keep fresher acidity and give tighter, more mineral wines, and white Châteauneuf does well.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 56.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 125 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Pignan
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit next to Rayas, on sandy soils among woods, straddling Châteauneuf-du-Pape and Courthézon. Château Rayas bottles a second Châteauneuf called Pignan from younger vines and lots, a lighter, perfumed Grenache in the Rayas style.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 54.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 70 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Chaban
appellations.summary: One of the highest lieux-dits of Cornas, at about 360 to 460 m on the plateau edge west of the village, on granite, cooler and later-ripening than the slopes above the village.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 56.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 360 to 460 m, with a mean slope of about 22%, facing east to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Eygas
appellations.summary: A large lieu-dit (often spelled Les Eygats) on the high slopes north-west of the village, at about 230 to 390 m, on granite. The higher ground gives fresher, more aromatic Cornas than the hot slopes by the village.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 60.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 385 m, with a mean slope of about 28%, facing broadly north-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Saint-Pierre
appellations.summary: A large lieu-dit on the slopes above Cornas, mostly facing south-east, on granite. Paul Jaboulet Aîné's Cornas Domaine de Saint-Pierre takes its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 55.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 275 to 405 m, with a mean slope of about 26%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Cornas is said to take its name from a Celtic word for 'burnt earth', a nod to its hot, south-facing amphitheatre.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Beau Renard Nord
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: Part of the Beau Renard sector east of the village, on gentle slopes of galets and clay. Domaine de Beaurenard, the Coulon family estate, takes its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 47.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Beau Renard is split into a north and a south part in the land register.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Vaudieu
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit south-east of the village, home of Château de Vaudieu, an eighteenth-century château built by an admiral of Louis XVI's navy, surrounded by vines on galets and sandy soils.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 49.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 85 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The papal summer castle that gave the village its name was built for John XXII in the fourteenth century; its ruined keep still dominates the vineyard.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Chapelle des Bois
appellations.summary: A climat in the south of Fleurie toward Morgon and Chiroubles, on granite sands. Clos de Mez bottles a Fleurie La Chapelle des Bois.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 46.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 275 to 335 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Fleurie is sometimes called the 'queen of Beaujolais' for its perfume and grace.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Madone
appellations.summary: The granite hill above Fleurie village, crowned by the nineteenth-century chapel of La Madone. Its slopes face south-east and east on pink granite sands, at about 330 to 430 m, and give the classic Fleurie: floral, silky and bright. La Madone is one of the lieux-dits in Fleurie's premier cru application. Domaine de la Madone and Domaine Chignard bottle it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 52.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 335 to 430 m, with a mean slope of about 20%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Javernières
appellations.summary: A climat at the foot of the Côte du Py, where the hill's schist meets clay and iron-rich deposits. Javernières combines the power of the Py with more flesh; Louis-Claude Desvignes's Javernières is the best-known bottling.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 52.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Au Michelon
appellations.summary: A large climat in Chénas on higher, south-facing slopes, at about 280 to 365 m, the northern part of the cru.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 45.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 280 to 365 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Au Michelon is one of the larger named climats of the cru, in the commune of Chénas.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Chapouin
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A flat lieu-dit in Courthézon on sandy soils. Domaine de la Janasse's Cuvée Chaupin, a pure old-vine Grenache, takes its name and fruit from here and shows the perfumed, supple side of sand-grown Grenache.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 42.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 55 to 60 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Sandy soils of the Courthézon side ripen Grenache more slowly than the pebble plateaus, which is why several estates keep their sand-grown old vines separate.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Crau
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary:
La Crau is the high, exposed plateau in the east of Châteauneuf-du-Pape, the classic image of the appellation: a thick layer of *galets roulés*, rounded quartzite pebbles left by the ancient Rhône, over red clay. The stones store the day's heat and protect the soil from drying, the clay holds water for dry summers, and the mistral blows through unhindered. Grenache here gives powerful, spicy, long-lived wine with garrigue and kirsch.

The plateau runs across the commune boundary into Bédarrides and Courthézon (mapped as separate La Crau units). Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe, named after the optical telegraph tower Claude Chappe built on the plateau in 1821, Domaine du Pegau and Henri Bonneau's Réserve des Célestins draw on La Crau.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 37.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 95 to 125 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, facing broadly south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The Brunier family of Vieux Télégraphe have farmed the plateau since 1891; their estate takes its name from the Chappe telegraph station that stood on La Crau.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Crau Sud (Courthézon)
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: The part of the La Crau plateau that lies in Courthézon, north of the Bédarrides sector, on galets over clay and sand.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 41.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 65 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, facing north to north-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Champagne
appellations.summary: A large climat of Fleurie on gentle slopes south-east of the village, on pink granite sand. Its name, like other Champagnes in Burgundy and Beaujolais, means open country (Latin *campania*).
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 43.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Moriers
appellations.summary: A climat in the north of Fleurie toward Moulin-à-Vent, on granite with some clay, facing east. Michel Chignard's Les Moriers is a reference for structured, age-worthy Fleurie.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 42.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 345 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Les Moriers lies next to Moulin-à-Vent, and its wines share some of their neighbour's structure.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Château-Gaillard
appellations.summary: A climat west of Villié-Morgon on gentle south-east-facing slopes. Clos de Mez bottles a Morgon Château Gaillard.
appellations.terroir: Gentle slopes of decomposed granite and schist on the western side of Villié-Morgon. The lieu-dit's 36.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 275 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Pizay
appellations.summary: The southern part of Morgon around the Château de Pizay, a hotel and wine estate, on low, gentle land of granite sand and alluvium.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 38.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 240 m, with a mean slope of about 4%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Morgon is the second-largest Beaujolais cru after Brouilly, with about 1,100 ha, which is why its climats matter for telling its wines apart.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Font de Michelle
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit in Bédarrides on the eastern edge of the appellation, on slopes facing east toward the Ouvèze. Domaine Font de Michelle, the Gonnet family estate, takes its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 30.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 60 to 100 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Vieux Télégraphe and Font de Michelle are both based in Bédarrides, one of the five communes of the appellation.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Crau Ouest (Bédarrides)
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: The part of the La Crau plateau that lies in the commune of Bédarrides, on the same deep layer of galets over red clay. Much of Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe's vineyard is in this sector, around the site of the old telegraph tower.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 26.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 100 to 110 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Pierre à Feu
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit whose name ('fire stone') refers to flint and quartzite stones that spark when struck, a nod to the galets that cover much of Châteauneuf-du-Pape.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 34.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 30 to 40 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, facing broadly west-south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Presle
appellations.summary: A steep climat of Fleurie, at about 330 to 445 m on granite, among the steepest slopes of the cru.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 29.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 325 to 445 m, with a mean slope of about 26%, facing north-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Garants
appellations.summary: A climat in the north of Fleurie on south-west-facing slopes of granite. Pierre-Marie Chermette's Domaine du Vissoux bottles Les Garants, a deeper style of Fleurie.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 31.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 265 to 340 m, with a mean slope of about 14%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Fleurie lies on a single commune, and almost all of it is planted on pink granite sand, which explains its floral, silky style.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Montgenas
appellations.summary: A climat on the slopes north-west of Fleurie village, at about 300 to 370 m, on pink granite; one of the higher, cooler named sites of the cru.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 34.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 305 to 365 m, with a mean slope of about 19%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Vers la Mont
appellations.summary: A large climat on the slopes rising from Fleurie village toward the chapel hill of La Madone, at about 300 to 430 m on granite, facing south-east.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 33.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 430 m, with a mean slope of about 19%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Corcelette
appellations.summary: A climat in the north-west of Morgon on sandy, pink granite, higher and lighter than the Côte du Py. Corcelette gives perfumed, silky Morgon; Jean Foillard's Corcelette, Daniel Bouland's old-vine bottling and Mee Godard's are admired.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 27.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 390 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Grand Cras
appellations.summary: A climat in the south of Morgon on clay, gravel and granite. Mee Godard bottles a Grand Cras, and Marcel Lapierre's family vineyards include parcels here.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 34.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 265 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Marcel Lapierre, Jean Foillard, Guy Breton and Jean-Paul Thévenet, the 'gang of four' of natural Beaujolais in the 1980s, all worked in Villié-Morgon, following the ideas of the négociant and scientist Jules Chauvet.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Au Mont
appellations.summary: A climat high on the Chénas hillside, at about 315 to 400 m on granite, among the highest land of Moulin-à-Vent.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 35.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 315 to 400 m, with a mean slope of about 17%, facing broadly east-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Champ de Cour
appellations.summary: A south-facing climat below the windmill on granite with clay; its wines are rich and deep. Château des Jacques, Richard Rottiers, Château du Moulin-à-Vent and Domaine Labruyère bottle Champ de Cour separately.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 28.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 220 to 245 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Vieux Bourg
appellations.summary: A climat around the old village core of Chénas, on higher granite slopes at about 290 to 375 m. The upper slopes of Chénas give firmer, cooler Moulin-à-Vent than the gentle land near the windmill.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 30.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 375 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, facing broadly east-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Chêne Marchand
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: A famous lieu-dit of Bué on gentle, south-east-facing slopes of *caillottes*, the hard, stony Oxfordian limestone that gives Sancerre its tense, flinty style. Le Chêne Marchand is bottled by several Bué estates, among them Jean-Max Roger, and is one of the classic names of the village.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 27.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Grand Chemarin
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit of Bué beside Chêne Marchand, on limestone (*caillottes*) and *terres blanches*, facing south-east. Le Grand Chemarin and its neighbour Petit Chemarin are among the most cited sites of the village.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 29.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Bué and Chavignol are the two most famous villages of the Sancerre appellation, which covers 14 communes.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Côte des Montdamnes
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary:
The main slope of the Monts Damnés above the hamlet of Chavignol, a very steep amphitheatre of Kimmeridgian marl (*terres blanches*) facing south and south-east. The slope is so hard to work that it was said to be 'damned', and it gives the most powerful, long-lived Sancerre: dense, chalky and saline, often opening after five or ten years.

François and Pascal Cotat, whose late-picked, barrel-fermented wines from Les Monts Damnés, La Grande Côte and Les Culs de Beaujeu are cult bottles, Gérard Boulay, and Henri Bourgeois (Le MD de Bourgeois) farm here.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 32.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 240 to 330 m, with a mean slope of about 26%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The same Kimmeridgian marl, with tiny fossil oysters (Exogyra virgula), runs under Chablis, about 120 km to the north-east.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Montée de Saint-Romble
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: A large lieu-dit in Sury-en-Vaux on slopes facing north and north-west, named after Saint Romble, a local hermit saint; its cooler exposure gives tense, citrus-driven Sauvignon.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 29.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 295 m, with a mean slope of about 19%, mostly north-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Crau Est (Bédarrides)
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: The eastern edge of the La Crau plateau in Bédarrides, where the galet-covered terrace begins to slope toward the Ouvèze. The same deep pebbles over red clay as the rest of La Crau.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 85 to 110 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Font du Loup (Courthézon)
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit in Courthézon on sandy and clay slopes facing north-east, home of Château de la Font du Loup, whose wines are known for their elegance rather than power.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 65 to 105 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
producers: Château de la Font du Loup
appellations.nerd_note: Font du Loup ('wolf's spring') is split between Courthézon and Bédarrides in the land register.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Gardine
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit west of the village on gentle slopes of galets and clay, home of Château La Gardine, the Brunel family estate, whose Cuvée des Générations comes from old vines here.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 25.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 75 to 105 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, facing south-west to west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Jannasse
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit in Courthézon, in the north-east of the appellation, which gave its name to Domaine de la Janasse, the Sabon family estate founded in 1973 and now one of the references of the appellation.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 45 to 55 m, with a mean slope of about 4%, facing south-west to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Nerthe
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: The lieu-dit of Château La Nerthe, one of the oldest estates of Châteauneuf-du-Pape, south-east of the village, whose history is documented from the sixteenth century. In the eighteenth century the Tulle de Villefranche family sold La Nerthe's wine under its own name, and Commandant Joseph Ducos rebuilt the vineyard after phylloxera, studying the role of each variety.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 19.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 90 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Brusquières
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A flat lieu-dit on the high plateau of the appellation, at about 110 to 125 m, on galets over clay and sand. Domaine de la Charbonnière's Les Hautes Brusquières, a dense, spicy Châteauneuf, comes from this sector.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 110 to 125 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Verlieu
appellations.summary: A large lieu-dit in Chavanay, the southern part of the Condrieu appellation, on steep granite slopes facing south-east. Chavanay is also part of Saint-Joseph, so its growers make both Viognier and Syrah.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 165 to 265 m, with a mean slope of about 39%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Château-Grillet, a tiny Viognier appellation of its own, is enclosed within Condrieu at Vérin.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Condrieu AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Condrieu when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Chaillot
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit at the northern edge of Cornas, on granite with a sandy topsoil (*gore*), facing south-east and east. It is the source of Thierry Allemand's Chaillot, the more aromatic of his two Cornas, and of Franck Balthazar's Chaillot.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 29%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Mazards
appellations.summary: A gently sloping lieu-dit at the foot of the Cornas slopes near the village, on deeper soils with alluvium and granite debris, which give rounder, earlier wines than the terraces above.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 175 m, with a mean slope of about 12%, facing east to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The lower, flatter lieux-dits near the Rhône give rounder Cornas, often blended with the granite terraces.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Reynard
appellations.summary: A steep granite slope just above the village of Cornas, facing south and south-east, worked on terraces. Reynard is the most famous lieu-dit of the appellation, made famous by Thierry Allemand's Cornas Reynard, a dense, mineral Syrah made without added sulphur in some vintages. Auguste Clape also uses Reynard fruit, and the Geynale parcel, made famous by Robert Michel and farmed by his nephew Vincent Paris, lies on this hillside.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 22.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 300 m, with a mean slope of about 38%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Côte Rozier
appellations.summary: A steep, south-east-facing slope in the north of the appellation, below the Rozier plateau, on schist. Côte Rozier is one of the classic sites of the northern Côte-Rôtie, giving dark, firm, spicy wines, and its fruit goes into several famous blends as well as single-site bottlings.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 40%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Coteaux de Bassenon
appellations.summary: The southernmost slopes of Côte-Rôtie, in Tupin-et-Semons toward Condrieu, facing south and south-west. The soils are granitic, as in Condrieu next door, and some Viognier grows among the Syrah, as the Côte-Rôtie rules allow.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 19.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 155 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 37%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Fongeant
appellations.summary: A broad lieu-dit on the upper slopes of Ampuis, facing south and south-west. Fongeant is one of the parcels Michel et Stéphane Ogier have bottled separately to show the variety of their Côte-Rôtie holdings.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 330 m, with a mean slope of about 25%, facing south-west to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Viallière
appellations.summary: A steep slope in the north of the appellation toward Vérenay, facing south-east, on schist with some granite. La Viallière gives perfumed, structured Côte-Rôtie with a bright, peppery line. It has become one of the most frequently named lieux-dits on labels: René Rostaing, Clusel-Roch, Domaine de Bonserine and Michel et Stéphane Ogier all bottle it separately.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 185 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 37%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Rozier
appellations.summary: The plateau and upper slopes above the Côte Rozier in the north of the appellation, at about 300 to 330 m. The higher, gentler land was planted later than the steep coteaux and gives a fresher, lighter style; it shows how Côte-Rôtie's vineyards have spread from the steep coteaux onto the higher, gentler ground.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 330 m, with a mean slope of about 17%, facing south-west to west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Fonfotin
appellations.summary: One of the highest climats of Fleurie, at about 375 to 460 m on granite, facing south-east and south-west, on the hills west of the village.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 21.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 375 to 460 m, with a mean slope of about 24%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Vivier
appellations.summary: A climat on the lower, gentle land of Fleurie at about 225 to 250 m, on granite sand and alluvium toward the Saône plain.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 21.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: L'Hermite
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: The top of the hill around the chapel of Saint-Christophe and the hermit's cell that gave Hermitage its name, with thinner, sandy granite soils (*arzelle*). It gives perfumed, finely structured red and fine, mineral white. Chapoutier's L'Ermite is a single-site red and white; Jean-Louis Chave also farms here.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 175 to 270 m, with a mean slope of about 29%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The legend says the knight Gaspard de Stérimberg retired to a hermitage on the hill in 1224 after the Albigensian Crusade and planted vines there.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Croix
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: Lower slopes on the eastern side of the hill near the town of Tain, on loess and pebbles; a source of supple red and white for blends.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 190 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Up to 15% of white Marsanne and Roussanne may be co-fermented with red Hermitage, though few growers use it.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Méal
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary:
In the middle of the hill, facing south, on limestone-rich pebbles and loess over granite; warm and rich, Le Méal gives ripe, sumptuous red and white. Its rounded stones are glacial and river deposits left on the slope, and they store heat.

Chapoutier bottles Le Méal separately as red and white, Paul Jaboulet Aîné's La Chapelle draws on it, and Marc Sorrel's Le Gréal blends Le Méal with Les Greffieux.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 140 to 225 m, with a mean slope of about 32%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Bessards
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary:
Les Bessards is the steep western end of the hill of Hermitage, on granite, and the backbone of red Hermitage: its Syrah is dark, firm, tannic and very long-lived, with black fruit, violets and a mineral, almost graphite edge.

Almost every great Hermitage draws on it. Jean-Louis Chave builds his red around Bessards; Chapoutier's Le Pavillon and Paul Jaboulet Aîné's La Chapelle rely heavily on it; Delas bottles a Les Bessards. The granite here is the same rock as Saint-Joseph across the river, from which the Rhône cut off the hill.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 20.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 240 m, with a mean slope of about 32%, facing south-west to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Hermitage is a piece of the Massif Central: the granite of Les Bessards was separated from the west bank when the Rhône shifted its course east of the hill.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Aux Charmes
appellations.summary: Les Charmes (in the land register Aux Charmes) is a climat on the high, south-facing slopes in the west of Morgon, on granite sands, giving a lighter, more perfumed Morgon. Jean-Marc Burgaud bottles a Morgon Les Charmes.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 320 to 370 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Douby
appellations.summary: A climat east of Villié-Morgon below the Côte du Py, on schist and granite. Douby is regularly named among the historic climats of Morgon.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 250 to 300 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Old Morgon is said to 'morgonner': with age the best climats take on a kirsch and earthy depth that can recall Pinot Noir.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Fontriante
appellations.summary: A climat west of Villié-Morgon on slopes facing south-west and south-east, on granite sands; one of the named sites of the cru's western half, which gives fresher, more floral wines than the Côte du Py.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 270 to 315 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing broadly south-south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Clachet
appellations.summary: A climat on almost flat land below the Côte du Py, on schist-derived soils and clay, one of the named sites of the eastern Morgon around the hamlet of Le Clachet.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 21.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 260 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Montpelain
appellations.summary: A climat on the gentle, lower ground of Morgon toward the south and east, facing north-east, on sandy granite and alluvial soils that give supple, early-drinking Gamay.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Saint-Joseph
appellations.summary: The highest climat of Morgon, at about 425 to 470 m on the western hills toward Chiroubles, on granite. It is a cool, late-ripening corner of the cru (not to be confused with the Rhône appellation of the same name).
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 19.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 425 to 470 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing broadly east-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Aux Caves
appellations.summary: A climat in Chénas on south-east-facing slopes at about 260 to 305 m, in the northern part of Moulin-à-Vent, on granite.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 255 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Rochelle
appellations.summary: A climat in Chénas on higher, south-east-facing slopes with thin granite soils. La Rochelle gives one of the most mineral, firmly built Moulin-à-Vents; Château du Moulin-à-Vent and Olivier Merlin bottle it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 265 to 310 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Burdelines
appellations.summary: A climat in Romanèche-Thorins on slopes facing north-east, on granite, one of the larger named sites of the cru.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 22.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 205 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Manganese in the granite of Moulin-à-Vent is often credited with the structure and longevity of its wines, though the link has never been proven.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Thorins
appellations.summary: Les Thorins, just north of the windmill, is one of the finest climats of Moulin-à-Vent and gave its name to the commune of Romanèche-Thorins. Its pink granite, crossed by veins of manganese, gives deep, structured Gamay that ages like Burgundy. Before the 1936 AOC the wines of the area were often sold as 'Thorins'. Louis Jadot's Château des Jacques bottles a Clos des Thorins.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 265 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Verillats
appellations.summary: A climat in Chénas north of the windmill, on granite. Château du Moulin-à-Vent's Croix des Vérillats takes its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 255 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, facing north-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Château du Moulin-à-Vent, owned by the Parinet family since 2009, bottles several climats separately.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Paradis (Mauves)
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit at Mauves, one of the original Saint-Joseph communes. Pierre Coursodon's Paradis Saint-Pierre, a long-lived red, takes part of its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 315 m, with a mean slope of about 42%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Mauves was one of the six original Saint-Joseph communes of 1956, with Glun, Tournon, Saint-Jean-de-Muzols, Lemps and Vion.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Saint-Joseph AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Saint-Joseph when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Saint - Joseph
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: The hillside at Tournon that gave its name to the whole appellation: the Jesuits of Tournon owned a vineyard here called 'Clos de Saint-Joseph', whose wine was known in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. When the AOC was created in 1956 it covered only six communes around Tournon and Mauves; it was later extended along 50 km of the west bank.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 38%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Saint-Joseph AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Saint-Joseph when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Romains
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit near Sancerre, facing south-west, on flinty clay (*silex*), a name linked by local tradition to Roman remains. Domaine Vacheron's Les Romains, from biodynamically farmed vines, is the reference: smoky, precise and long.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 14%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Petit Chemarin
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: The smaller neighbour of Grand Chemarin in Bué, on south-east-facing slopes of limestone (*caillottes*) and *terres blanches*; one of the cluster of famous Bué lieux-dits with Chêne Marchand.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 255 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing broadly east-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Marigny
appellations.summary: A large lieu-dit on the plateau above Vouvray, on clay with flint (*perruches*) over tuffeau, the classic soils of the Vouvray plateau above the Loire.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Petite Crau
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A small lieu-dit in Bédarrides at the edge of the La Crau plateau, sharing its pebble-covered terrace soils.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 65 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Roquette
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A small lieu-dit north-east of the village, next to Rayas and Pignan, where sandy soils dominate. Domaine La Roquette, owned by the Brunier family of Vieux Télégraphe since 1986, takes its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 7.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 110 to 125 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Solitude
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit south of the village, home of Domaine de la Solitude, owned by the Lançon family, descendants of the Barberini family that came to the papal Comtat in the seventeenth century.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 85 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Bois de Boursan
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A low-lying lieu-dit in the south of the appellation, near the Sorgues side, which gave its name to Domaine Bois de Boursan, known for its traditional Châteauneuf.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 30 to 40 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's decree names 13 varieties (18 counting colour variants), but Grenache dominates the vineyard.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Cristia (Courthézon)
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit in Courthézon on the sandy, gently sloping eastern side of the appellation, which gave its name to Domaine de Cristia, the Grangeon family estate.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 60 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 13%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The appellation covers five communes: Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Courthézon, Bédarrides, Orange and Sorgues.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Grès
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A small lieu-dit in Courthézon whose name refers to sandstone (*grès*) and sand rather than the famous pebbles. On sandy soils Grenache ripens more slowly and keeps more perfume and finesse, which is why sand-grown Châteauneuf, as at nearby Rayas, is prized by growers looking for elegance.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 60 to 100 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing east to north-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Rayas
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary:
The lieu-dit of Château Rayas, the most singular estate in Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Unlike the stony plateaus, Rayas lies on sandy soils (weathered sandstone) in clearings among pine and oak woods, on slopes that face north. Cool, sheltered and low-yielding, it gives Grenache of extraordinary perfume and transparency, closer to great Burgundy than to the dark, heady style of the appellation.

The Reynaud family has owned Rayas since the late nineteenth century; Jacques Reynaud made it a cult wine, and his nephew Emmanuel Reynaud ran it from 1997 until his death in November 2025, also making Château des Tours and Château de Fonsalette.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 15.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 65 to 110 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing broadly north (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Château Rayas red is essentially pure Grenache from old vines, rare in an appellation of blends.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Village
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: The vineyards around the village of Châteauneuf-du-Pape and below the ruined papal castle, built for Pope John XXII in the fourteenth century as a summer residence, on the slopes of limestone and sand that surround the hilltop.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 20%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Relagnes
appellations.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit west of the village on slopes facing west toward the Rhône. Domaine des Relagnes, the Boiron family estate, takes its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 13.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 55 to 85 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing west to north-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The western slopes toward the Rhône have more sand and clay and fewer pebbles than the eastern plateaus.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Chéry
appellations.summary: One of the great Condrieu slopes, just south of the town, facing south on granite with a topsoil of weathered mica and sand (*arzelle*). Chéry gives rich but precise Viognier, with apricot and violet and a stony finish. André Perret's Coteau de Chéry is a reference, and several other growers bottle it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 185 to 260 m, with a mean slope of about 40%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Condrieu shrank to about 8 ha in the mid-1960s; growers such as Georges Vernay replanted the terraces, and today it has around 200 ha.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Condrieu AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Condrieu when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Vernon
appellations.summary: The steep granite slope above the town of Condrieu that includes the Coteau de Vernon, source of Georges Vernay's most famous Viognier, from vines planted in the 1930s and 1940s. The wine is mineral, tight and long-lived, a rebuttal to the idea that Condrieu must be drunk young.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 43%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Condrieu AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Condrieu when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Champelrose
appellations.summary: A small, east-facing lieu-dit on the lower slopes near the village, where limestone appears among the granite. Domaine Courbis bottles a Cornas Champelrose, a rounder counterpart to its La Sabarotte.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 165 m, with a mean slope of about 12%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Cornas has been pure Syrah since its AOC of 1938; no white grapes or Viognier are allowed.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Chavaroche
appellations.summary: A steep lieu-dit of the Côte Brune above Ampuis, on dark schist. Bernard Levet's La Chavaroche, from old vines and made with whole bunches in old casks, is a reference for the wild, savoury, traditional side of Côte-Rôtie.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 205 to 310 m, with a mean slope of about 39%, facing south-west to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Cognet
appellations.summary: A steep, south-facing slope in Ampuis, one of the parcels bottled separately by Michel et Stéphane Ogier.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 275 m, with a mean slope of about 35%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Côte-Rôtie allows up to 20% Viognier, co-fermented with the Syrah, a tradition from the days of mixed plantings.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Côte Bodin
appellations.summary: A steep slope in Ampuis facing south-east and east, bottled as a single lieu-dit by Michel et Stéphane Ogier.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 180 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 39%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The Ogiers' 2019 'sélection de lieux-dits' bottled nine single sites, an unusual exercise in a region where most wines are blends of several slopes.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Côte Brune
appellations.summary:
The cadastral Côte Brune is a small, very steep lieu-dit above Ampuis that gave its name to the whole northern half of Côte-Rôtie. Legend says the Seigneur de Maugiron left his slopes to two daughters, one dark and one fair, hence Côte Brune and Côte Blonde. The brown, iron-rich schist here gives firm, dark, savoury Syrah that needs a decade.

Domaine Jamet's Côte Brune is the modern reference, and the Gentaz-Dervieux Côte Brune of the 1970s to 1990s is a legend among collectors; Gilles Barge also bottles a Côte Brune.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 170 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 43%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Coteaux de Tupin
appellations.summary: Steep slopes in Tupin-et-Semons, the southern commune of Côte-Rôtie, facing south-east and south. The southern sector has more granite and gneiss than the Côte Brune, and the wines are finer and more perfumed, closer to the Côte Blonde style.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 14.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 180 to 310 m, with a mean slope of about 48%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Grandes Places
appellations.summary: Les Grandes Places is a steep slope in the north of Côte-Rôtie, near Vérenay, on dark schist. Clusel-Roch's Les Grandes Places, from old vines of the local Sérine selection of Syrah, is one of the most admired traditional Côte-Rôties, dense and spicy; Jean-Michel Gerin also makes a Grandes Places.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 270 to 325 m, with a mean slope of about 24%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Sérine is the old, small-berried Syrah selection of the northern Rhône; several growers propagate it by massal selection from their own vines.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Landonne
appellations.summary:
La Landonne is the most famous lieu-dit of the Côte Brune, the northern half of Côte-Rôtie, on a slope so steep (the terrain model averages about 50%) that it is worked on narrow terraces held by dry-stone walls. Its dark mica-schist, rich in iron oxides, gives the most powerful, tannic and long-lived wines of the appellation: black fruit, smoke, olive and iron, with little of the floral lift of the southern slopes.

Marcel Guigal assembled La Landonne from dozens of small plots in the 1970s and released the first Guigal La Landonne with the 1978 vintage; with La Mouline and La Turque it forms the trio of 'La La' wines that made Côte-Rôtie world-famous in the 1980s. Unlike its siblings it is pure Syrah. René Rostaing, Jean-Michel Gerin and Delas also bottle La Landonne.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 4.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 185 to 270 m, with a mean slope of about 50%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Guigal's La Turque comes from the Côte Brune and La Mouline from the Côte Blonde; neither name is a cadastral lieu-dit, which is why they do not appear as separate units on this map.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Lancement
appellations.summary: A slope in the south of Ampuis on the Côte Blonde side, where lighter, more granitic soils give finer, more aromatic wine. Michel et Stéphane Ogier's Lancement is one of the estate's flagship wines: perfumed, silky and long.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 340 m, with a mean slope of about 25%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Champon
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit on the upper, gentler ground of Ampuis near the plateau, at about 310 to 340 m. Michel et Stéphane Ogier bottle Le Champon separately; the higher position gives a lighter, more aromatic style.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 305 to 340 m, with a mean slope of about 18%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Mollard
appellations.summary: A steep slope in Ampuis facing south-east, worked on terraces of schist; one of the many lieux-dits whose fruit goes into the blends of the Ampuis growers.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 170 to 290 m, with a mean slope of about 46%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Many Côte-Rôtie lieux-dits are farmed in tiny parcels by several growers, so their names appear mainly in blends.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Leyat
appellations.summary: A slope in Ampuis on the Côte Brune side. Leyat is one of the parcels Michel et Stéphane Ogier have bottled as a single lieu-dit in their 'sélection de lieux-dits'.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 250 to 315 m, with a mean slope of about 28%, facing broadly east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Most Côte-Rôtie estates own small parcels in several lieux-dits and blend them; single-lieu-dit bottlings are a recent trend.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Montlis
appellations.summary: A steep lieu-dit in Saint-Cyr-sur-le-Rhône, the northern commune of Côte-Rôtie, facing south-east. Montlis is one of the single-lieu-dit wines of Michel et Stéphane Ogier, and shows the cooler, fresher side of the northern extension of the appellation.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 175 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 38%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
