appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Montmain
appellations.summary: A steep, south-facing slope in Ampuis, one of the lieux-dits Michel et Stéphane Ogier bottle separately. Steep schist and full sun give dark, concentrated Syrah.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 190 to 310 m, with a mean slope of about 41%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The appellation runs along about 8 km of the right bank, on the communes of Saint-Cyr-sur-le-Rhône, Ampuis and Tupin-et-Semons.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Rochins
appellations.summary: A steep lieu-dit of the Côte Brune above Ampuis, facing south-west, on dark schist. Domaine Garon bottles Les Rochins, and Patrick and Christophe Bonnefond's 'Les Rochains' comes from the same slope.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 180 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 42%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: 'Les Rochains' and 'Rochins' are two spellings of the same place, a common confusion in northern Rhône names.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Vérenay
appellations.summary: The lower slopes around the hamlet of Vérenay, at the northern end of the Ampuis commune, where Côte-Rôtie's northern coteaux begin. Several growers are based in the hamlet, including Clusel-Roch.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 155 to 180 m, with a mean slope of about 19%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Vérenay marks the northern end of the Côte Brune slopes; the hamlet sits at the foot of the coteaux.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Grand'Cour
appellations.summary: A small climat around the Clos de la Grand'Cour, the Dutraive family's walled estate, a reference of the natural wine school of Beaujolais.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 7.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 285 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Jean-Louis Dutraive farms the walled Clos de la Grand'Cour organically and makes his wines with whole bunches and little or no sulphur.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Grille Midi Nord
appellations.summary: The northern part of Grille-Midi, a steep, sun-trap slope ('grill at noon') above the village. Grille-Midi is one of the best-known Fleurie climats, giving ripe, intense Gamay.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 315 to 410 m, with a mean slope of about 18%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Grille-Midi is split into a north and a south part in the land register; both are mapped here.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Grille Midi Sud
appellations.summary: The southern part of Grille-Midi, the sun-trap slope above Fleurie village (the name means 'grill at noon'); one of the best-known climats of the cru.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 310 to 360 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing north-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Roilette
appellations.summary: A climat bordering Moulin-à-Vent with more clay than most of Fleurie, known for the Coudert family's Clos de la Roilette, whose fuller, firmer wine was long sold as Fleurie but tastes closer to its neighbour.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 275 m, with a mean slope of about 14%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Beaume
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit in the middle of the eastern hill, on stony limestone soils mixed with loess. Beaume is part of Jean-Louis Chave's red blend and gives warm, round Syrah.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 7.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 185 m, with a mean slope of about 27%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Jean-Louis Chave blends his red Hermitage from parcels in several lieux-dits rather than bottling them separately, a deliberate choice for complexity.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Diognières et Torras
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit at the foot of the eastern hill that combines Diognières and Torras, on stony alluvial ground, giving supple, ripe Syrah for blends.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 4.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 140 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Hermitage was famous enough in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries for Bordeaux merchants to add it to their clarets, a practice known as 'hermitager'.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Diognières
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: Flat to gently sloping land at the foot of the eastern hill, on deep, stony alluvium. Les Diognières gives rounder, fleshier red; Ferraton bottles a Les Dionnières, and Chave includes it in his blend.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 130 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Grandes Vignes
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: The part of the Hermitage AOC that lies in the commune of Crozes-Hermitage, north-east of the main hill, on higher slopes at about 250 to 320 m. It is a reminder that the appellation's limits follow terroir rather than commune boundaries.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 250 to 320 m, with a mean slope of about 33%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Greffieux
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: At the bottom of the hill below Le Méal and Les Bessards, on silty alluvium and scree washed down the slope. Its Syrah is supple, aromatic and earlier-drinking, the softening element of many blends. Marc Sorrel (in Le Gréal) and Chapoutier make single-site versions.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 120 to 150 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Murets
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: On the eastern part of the hill, on loess (wind-blown silt) over granite and limestone, facing south. Les Murets is a classic white-wine site; Chapoutier's De l'Orée white comes from here, and the name Chante-Alouette is traditionally linked to this part of the hill.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 185 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Rocoules
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit in the east of the hill on loess and limestone, famous for white Hermitage from Marsanne and Roussanne. Chave and Marc Sorrel use it, and Sorrel's white Les Rocoules is a single-site bottling of great longevity.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 185 m, with a mean slope of about 22%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Maison Blanche
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit on the eastern, gentler part of the hill around a white house, on loess and limestone pebbles. Its Marsanne gives rich, honeyed white Hermitage, and Chave's white blend includes Maison Blanche.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 185 to 200 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Roche
appellations.summary: A small climat on a rocky (*roche*) shoulder of the Morgon hills at about 320 to 335 m, on granite.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 320 to 335 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Carquelin
appellations.summary: A climat in Romanèche-Thorins below the windmill. Château des Jacques's Clos du Grand Carquelin and Domaine Labruyère's Le Carquelin come from this sector.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 220 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Moulin-à-Vent is often aged in oak barrels, Burgundy-style, and its best climats can keep for ten years or more.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Champagne
appellations.summary: A climat in Chénas on gentle granite slopes; the name, common in Burgundy and Beaujolais, comes from the Latin *campania*, open country, and has nothing to do with the sparkling wine region.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 15.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Roche
appellations.summary: A climat in Romanèche-Thorins near the windmill, on thin, rocky granite (hence the name). Château des Jacques and Thibault Liger-Belair bottle La Roche.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing east to north-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Romanèche-Thorins is also home to the Hameau du Vin, the wine museum and park created by Georges Duboeuf.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Tour du Bief
appellations.summary: A climat in Chénas on gentle granite slopes; Domaine de la Tour du Bief takes its name from it.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 13.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 255 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
producers: Domaine de la Tour du Bief
appellations.nerd_note: Moulin-à-Vent straddles two communes, Romanèche-Thorins in Saône-et-Loire and Chénas in the Rhône, and so two départements.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Moulin à Vent
appellations.summary: The climat around the sixteenth-century windmill on its hilltop at Romanèche-Thorins, a listed historic monument that gave the cru its name. The pink granite here is famous for its veins of manganese.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 240 to 260 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Moulin-à-Vent is the only Beaujolais cru named after a monument rather than a village.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Perrelles
appellations.summary: One of the lowest climats of Moulin-à-Vent, in Romanèche-Thorins at about 190 to 210 m, on sandy granite and alluvium toward the Saône plain.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 190 to 210 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Rouchaux
appellations.summary: A climat in Romanèche-Thorins on gentle slopes facing east, on granite sand. Thibault Liger-Belair, the Nuits-Saint-Georges grower who bought in Moulin-à-Vent in 2009, bottles Les Rouchaux.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 15.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 205 to 225 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Several Côte d'Or growers have invested in Moulin-à-Vent since the 2000s, drawn by its granite climats and modest land prices.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Rochenoire
appellations.summary: The highest climat of the cru, in Chénas at about 365 to 425 m, on dark granite ('black rock'), facing south.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 365 to 425 m, with a mean slope of about 24%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Higher climats such as Rochenoire ripen later and have gained attention in the warm vintages since the 2010s.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Oliviers
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A lieu-dit at Tournon. Pierre Gonon's white Saint-Joseph Les Oliviers, from Marsanne and Roussanne, is one of the best whites of the northern Rhône.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 175 m, with a mean slope of about 21%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: White Saint-Joseph is made from Marsanne and Roussanne, and is a small share of the appellation.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Saint-Joseph AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Saint-Joseph when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Sainte-Épine
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A steep granite slope at Saint-Jean-de-Muzols, north of Tournon, and one of the historic heartlands of Saint-Joseph. Delas's Saint-Joseph Sainte-Épine, from old vines, is its best-known bottling: firm, dark and peppery.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 215 m, with a mean slope of about 35%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The granite hills between Tournon and Saint-Jean-de-Muzols are the historic heart of Saint-Joseph, before the appellation was stretched to 26 communes.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Saint-Joseph AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Saint-Joseph when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Poussie
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: A steep amphitheatre above Bué, facing south-west, on Kimmeridgian marl: one of the most spectacular slopes of the appellation, long famous through the Cordier family's Château de la Poussie.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 305 to 350 m, with a mean slope of about 30%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Sancerre's three main soils are terres blanches (Kimmeridgian marl), caillottes (stony limestone) and silex (flinty clay), and growers often blend all three.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Cul de Beaujeu
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: A very steep slope above Chavignol, facing south-east, on Kimmeridgian marl: one of the trio of great Chavignol sites with the Monts Damnés and La Grande Côte. The Cotat cousins' Les Culs de Beaujeu and Lucien Crochet's Le Cul de Beaujeu are references.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 330 m, with a mean slope of about 33%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Clos du Bourg
appellations.summary: A walled vineyard in the heart of Vouvray, on shallow clay and limestone over tuffeau, bought by Domaine Huet in 1953. Often considered the greatest of Huet's sites, Clos du Bourg gives the most powerful and complete Chenin of the estate.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 85 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Haut Lieu
appellations.summary:
The plateau above Vouvray where Domaine Huet began: Victor Huet and his son Gaston bought Le Haut-Lieu in 1928. On deep clay over limestone (*argile à silex* over tuffeau), it gives the most open, supple of Huet's three single vineyards, in styles from sec to moelleux and sparkling depending on the year.

Gaston Huet, mayor of Vouvray for decades, made the estate a reference for Chenin Blanc; it converted to biodynamics in 1990.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 95 to 105 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Huet decides each vintage whether a site makes sec, demi-sec or moelleux, so the same vineyard can give three different wines in three years.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Mont
appellations.summary: A steep, south-facing slope at the edge of the tuffeau escarpment above the Loire, with thin, stony soils of flinty clay (*silex*) over limestone. Domaine Huet bought Le Mont in 1957; it gives its most mineral, tightly wound Vouvray, slow to open and very long-lived.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 7.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 60 to 100 m, with a mean slope of about 21%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Bertholon
appellations.summary: A small lieu-dit on the plateau above Ampuis, at about 330 m, bottled separately by Michel et Stéphane Ogier as an example of the fresher, higher-altitude Côte-Rôtie.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 1.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 325 to 335 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The plateau above the slopes is included in the AOC; its gentler, higher sites give lighter wines than the coteaux.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: La Brocarde
appellations.summary: A small, steep lieu-dit in Ampuis facing south-east, on the Côte Blonde side, where lighter, granitic soils give finer, more perfumed Syrah.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 4.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 165 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 35%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Côte-Rôtie's terraces are held by dry-stone walls; many were rebuilt after the vineyard shrank sharply in the mid-twentieth century.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Vercandière
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A small, flat lieu-dit at the foot of the hill, on alluvial soils, a source of supple Syrah for blends.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 1.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 120 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The lieux-dits at the foot of the hill are often blended with the steep sites to soften them.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Péléat
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A small, south-facing lieu-dit in the middle of the hill between Le Méal and L'Hermite, on loess and scree over granite. Péléat is one of the parcels in Jean-Louis Chave's red blend, contributing aromatic finesse.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 2.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 130 to 180 m, with a mean slope of about 17%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Torras et les Garennes
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: A small part of the Hermitage AOC in the commune of Larnage, on the eastern flank of the hill, where the white clay of Larnage begins.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 2.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 140 to 175 m, with a mean slope of about 30%, facing west to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Hermitage covers only about 137 ha, on the communes of Tain-l'Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage and Larnage.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Varogne
appellations.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
appellations.summary: The very steep western tip of the hill above the Rhône, facing west, on granite. Varogne is rarely named on labels but adds firm, dark Syrah to blends, close in style to Les Bessards.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 3.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 130 to 205 m, with a mean slope of about 50%, mostly west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Montdamnes
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: A small cadastral piece of the Monts Damnés slope above Chavignol, separate from the main Côte des Montdamnes, on the same steep Kimmeridgian marl.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 1.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 260 to 295 m, with a mean slope of about 32%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Les Monts Damnés
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
appellations.summary: The part of the Monts Damnés slope that lies in the commune of Verdigny, next to the main Côte des Montdamnes above Chavignol, on the same Kimmeridgian marl.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 3.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 285 to 325 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The Monts Damnés lieu-dit is split between the communes of Sancerre (Chavignol) and Verdigny in the land register.
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

appellations.name: Le Clos Baudoin
appellations.summary: A small walled vineyard (often spelled Clos Baudoin) on the slopes of Vouvray, once owned by the Poniatowski family and farmed by François Chidaine since 2006. His Clos Baudoin is a tense, mineral Vouvray from old vines.
appellations.terroir: The lieu-dit's 2.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 90 to 100 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.
